description: SDK-only reference vectors and lifecycle COVERAGE MANIFEST; lifecycle entries require native executable tests. Fake credential strings; no AHP wire-schema change. In token_responses, requested is the caller's requested set (within allowed for acquisitions; the original request for refreshes); a response scope that is absent, null or blank inherits like an omitted one; wire_request, present for exchange reacquire, is the scope set actually sent: previous_granted plus ceiling-filtered requested and required. client_selection inputs describe host configuration and authorization-server metadata; registration_responses use now as the current Unix time. registration_request_digests hash host registration policy; a record whose digest differs is unusable.

lifecycle.expect: valid stored grant works without metadata HTTP, including a recreated provider
known authorized binding sends stored token on first attempt; no 401/replay for upload or notification
401/insufficient_scope on a notification or upload is not replayed but runs challenge handling (discovery, client-credentials acquisition, no login creation); the next operation sends a credential
401 for a stored token with unknown or future expiry marks it stale and renews it, so the next operation does not resend the rejected token
up-front lookup never creates a pending login or performs protected-resource discovery; only a store miss or host policy refusal sends an anonymous attempt
up-front lookup refreshes an expired stored token non-interactively using cached authorization-server metadata
expired client-credentials token without refresh token is re-acquired non-interactively by the up-front lookup using persisted metadata
binding record lacking persisted authorization-server metadata fetches only the stored issuer's metadata, never protected-resource metadata; failure is discovery_failed

renewal failing before the token endpoint processed it (DNS, TCP connect, TLS handshake, token-endpoint 404/410) refetches the stored issuer's metadata once, persists it if the issuer is unchanged and retries once; changed issuer or failed refetch is discovery_failed

read timeout, reset after send, 5xx, non-OAuth body or OAuth error during renewal returns its error (provider_failed/retry for ambiguous failures) with no metadata refetch and no immediate retry; the presented refresh token is not replayed
known binding whose non-interactive refresh fails (transient, invalid_grant, missing cached metadata) fails the operation with that error, never sends anonymously
known PKCE binding whose tokens were dropped fails interaction_required at lookup; a later prepare restores it
rotated refresh credential persisted and reusable when expires_in absent
5xx/non-OAuth/timeout retains credentials and returns retry, never permanent fabricated login state
definitive interactive refresh invalid_grant removes access and refresh tokens when the record still holds the presented refresh token, and returns refresh_rejected
invalid_grant for a refresh token already replaced by a newer record leaves the newer record intact
invalid code-exchange response persists nothing; invalid refresh response persists only a valid rotated refresh token; no in-flight/refreshing state remains; returns provider_failed
retry can acquire with current client credentials without any human-login outcome
delivery/credential/challenge paths return interaction_required without creating a pending login; only explicit prepare creates one
pending login lifetime is host-configured and bounded (default 10 minutes), fixed at creation and survives the creating prepare's deadline or cancellation
a pending login created in one process completes from another process sharing the store

later prepare with same grant key and exact redirect whose requested+required scopes are within the pending scopes reuses it regardless of deadline or ceiling; completion records scopes bounded by the stored creating ceiling

later prepare with a different grant key or redirect, or scopes outside the pending scopes, supersedes it; a different grant key or redirect starts from the new caller's scopes and ceiling alone; old callback fails interaction_required

with the same grant key and redirect, a superseding login requests old pending scopes plus the new caller's ceiling-filtered requested+required scopes and stores the union of both ceilings; alternating callers with different ceilings converge
a pending login ends exactly once by completion, supersede, cancel or expiry; later callbacks fail interaction_required
nonidentity metadata, token-endpoint auth method and runtime secret changes do not permanently fail stored session or persist secret
widening the allowed ceiling finds the existing grant; effective scopes are granted scopes intersected with the current ceiling at use
narrowing the ceiling hides scopes at use only; after a refresh under the narrow ceiling and widening it again the scope is still available
only Bearer 403 insufficient_scope triggers allowed-scope step-up for the challenged operation
a challenge requirement is not persisted on the binding; later operations use the stored grant, including scopes added by step-up consent
step-up or re-acquisition requests previously granted plus new ceiling-filtered scopes and records response scopes within previously granted plus acquisition ceiling; earlier scopes are not lost
interaction_required carries the validated required scopes; host passes them to prepare as explicit required scopes and consent includes them; access_denied reports them for diagnostics only
prepare with explicit required scopes outside the caller's ceiling fails access_denied
401 or Bearer 403 insufficient_scope on hooks/intercept, hooks/configuration or hooks/capabilities replays once with the same request id and body; second rejection fails
explicit trusted preset uses issuer metadata and does not require PRM
independently approved event/upload bindings share consent only with same explicit grant partition
invalid state/redirect does not consume pending handle; subsequent valid callback can complete once
literal IPv4/IPv6 loopback HTTP redirect accepted; remote HTTP rejected
initial request read+write grants read; refresh with no scope stays read and cannot fabricate write
insufficient_scope without scope cannot invent permissions; require explicit host requirement or deny
initial read+write request grants read; refresh response scoped read write records read only, persists rotated refresh and stays usable; a write-requiring operation fails access_denied
response scopes outside the allowed ceiling (e.g. openid, offline_access) are dropped from the recorded grant, not an error

with every source available the SDK selects a pre-registered client, else CIMD (PKCE, client_id_metadata_document_supported true), else permitted DCR with registration_endpoint, else credential_unavailable

a host-supplied pre-registered client is used even when CIMD and DCR are available; adding one later makes a recorded CIMD/DCR selection obsolete, selecting a new grant key whose old tokens are never presented under the new client
PKCE with a configured CIMD URL and client_id_metadata_document_supported true sends the URL as client_id with no client secret, token auth none and no stored registration record
absent or non-true client_id_metadata_document_supported skips CIMD and uses permitted DCR
a redirect not exactly listed in the host-declared CIMD redirect_uris fails invalid_configuration before any pending login or registration
no SDK network request targets the CIMD URL or a URL derived from it
client_credentials never uses CIMD; it uses a pre-registered client or DCR with a secret-based method
invalid_client for a CIMD client is invalid_configuration and never triggers DCR for that operation
registration_endpoint advertised but host policy does not permit the exact issuer: no registration request; credential_unavailable
non-HTTPS, destination-policy-refused or redirecting registration endpoint sends no further request and fails untrusted_destination
a PKCE client is registered only by host prepare; client-credentials registration may occur in prepare and any non-interactive acquisition, including the up-front lookup and challenge handling
concurrent processes needing the same registration_key send one registration request; the compare-and-set loser deletes its secret reference and uses the winner's record
grants in different bindings or partitions with the same registration_key reuse one registration

a passed nonzero client_secret_expires_at or unresolvable secret reference makes the record unusable; client-credentials acquisition, including the up-front lookup, re-registers under coordination before any token-endpoint request

token-endpoint invalid_client for a DCR client compare-and-deletes that registration generation; where registration is allowed client credentials re-register once and re-acquire once; PKCE returns interaction_required and the next prepare registers anew; no metadata refetch
a replacement client_id yields a new grant key; the old grant is not migrated or presented; PKCE returns interaction_required, client credentials re-acquire
the client secret is written only through the host secret-storage hook; registration, binding, grant and pending-login records and errors never contain it
without a host secret-storage hook a client-credentials DCR fails credential_unavailable with no registration request; PKCE DCR is unaffected
newly advertised CIMD support or a removed registration_endpoint does not move a working grant off its recorded client
registration_access_token and registration_client_uri are ignored, never persisted and never used
a host initial access token configured for one exact issuer is sent only to that issuer's registration endpoint, never to another issuer's, and never persisted
the up-front lookup never registers a PKCE client and returns interaction_required when its registration is missing; for client credentials it may (re-)register under the failed-marker backoff

every failed registration outcome and a repeated invalid_client persist or update a failed marker with failure time, attempt count and next attempt time; until it elapses (default 1 minute doubling to 1 hour) no path but host prepare sends a registration request, across operations and processes; prepare, success or a request digest change clears it
a 2xx JSON registration response failing validation (secret for PKCE, replaced redirect, swapped auth method) persists nothing and returns invalid_configuration, not retry

prepare with the explicit force-registration option compare-and-deletes the current registration generation and its secret reference, clears a failed marker and registers anew; an expired pending login alone never triggers re-registration

a changed client_name, software identifier, registration scope or initial access token reference makes the record's request_digest stale; the record is compare-and-deleted and the next permitted registration uses the new policy

after a registration record is replaced or compare-and-deleted, the old secret reference is deleted through the host hook once the compare-and-set succeeds; a losing compare-and-set deletes only its own fresh reference

an unattended client-credentials host blocked by a failed marker sends no registration request during the backoff, then re-registers and acquires on the next operation after it elapses, without host prepare

a successful client-credentials acquisition whose client_secret_expires_at is within min(0.1 x (client_secret_expires_at - local registered_at), 1 hour) re-registers under coordination, so the scheduled expiry causes no outage; client_id_issued_at is not relied on
while a failed marker is active, a still-valid stored token is still sent and PKCE still returns interaction_required; only registration requests are suppressed

a pending login records its registration generation; invalid_client at its completion after a forced re-registration compare-and-deletes only that generation and leaves the newer registration, even with the same reissued client_id
5xx, 408, 429, network and 401/403 registration failures update the failed marker, so repeated lookups and notifications across processes send no registration request until the backoff elapses
a registration response with Retry-After sets the next attempt no earlier than Retry-After and no earlier than the exponential backoff, capped at the host maximum

under the registration-key lock each process reloads and checks the marker, then updates it by compare-and-set on its generation; concurrent failures increment the attempt count without loss and at most one process sends a registration request per permitted attempt
concurrent processes inside the renewal margin reload and re-check under the registration-key lock; exactly one sends a registration request and the others use its new record

a proactive re-registration failing (e.g. 5xx or 429) inside the renewal margin updates the failed marker, but the operation succeeds with the current still-usable registration and token until that registration actually expires

discovery answered 401 with no usable grant skips the backend and emits a host-visible diagnostic {backendId, code configuration_unavailable, authError interaction_required, recovery login}; no credentials or bodies; cancellation emits no diagnostic and propagates
after a successful host prepare for the skipped backend's event endpoint, the next event admission re-attempts discovery without waiting for backoff and admits the backend's routes

a configuration_unavailable skip with no authError, or with recovery retry, is re-attempted only at the first admission or initialize after backoff (30s, doubling, capped at 1h, host-configurable); earlier admissions do not contact the backend

a configuration_unavailable skip whose recovery is login, configure or none is not re-attempted when backoff elapses; only a successful host prepare for that backend's endpoint or reinitialization re-attempts it
configuration_invalid, no_applicable_subscriptions and configuration_local_secret skips are never re-attempted before reinitialization, even after prepare or backoff elapses
a retry runs inside the single shared admission: concurrent callers observe old or complete new routes, never partial; events admitted before the retry succeeded are not replayed
